messages.content:
Sarunyu has a stick of length 1 with one endpoint marked in red. Every minute, he picks one of his sticks uniformly at random and breaks it into two halves of equal length. Compute the expected length of the stick with the red endpoint after 5 minutes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(L_k\) be the length of the stick with the red endpoint after \(k\) minutes.

At the start of minute \(k\), there are \(k\) sticks total, and exactly one contains the red endpoint. So the red stick is chosen to be broken with probability

\[
\frac{1}{k}.
\]

If it is not chosen, its length stays the same. If it is chosen, its length is halved. Therefore,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_k \mid L_{k-1}]
=
\left(1-\frac1k\right)L_{k-1}
+
\frac1k\cdot \frac{L_{k-1}}2
=
\frac{2k-1}{2k}L_{k-1}.
\]

Taking expectations and starting with \(L_0=1\),

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\prod_{k=1}^5 \frac{2k-1}{2k}
=
\frac12\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac56\cdot\frac78\cdot\frac9{10}.
\]

Thus,

\[
\mathbb{E}[L_5]
=
\frac{945}{3840}
=
\frac{63}{256}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{63}{256}}
\]
